previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of COPD, congestive heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, diabetes, morbid obesity, and atrial fibrillation was admitted for left leg swelling present for two weeks. Evaluation revealed chronic venous insufficiency with early skin breakdown and signs of cellulitis, but no deep vein thrombosis on ultrasound. She was afebrile with stable vital signs and no evidence of acute heart failure, supported by low BNP and mild imaging changes. She was treated with antibiotics for cellulitis and advised to resume daily diuretic use. Compression therapy was recommended for venous insufficiency, and anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation was deferred pending cardiology follow-up. She improved clinically and was discharged to extended care with outpatient follow-up plans.

Brief Hospital Course:
Pt was seen in the Emergency Department on ___ for a RLE 
traumatic soft tissue wound following a fall.  She was noted at 
the time of admission to have a elevated Cr (1.8 from baseline 
0.9).  She was admitted to Vascular Surgery.  Her oral 
hypoglycemics were held, and she was gently hydrated.  Her wound 
was initially dressed with gauze and an ACE wrap.  On ___, 
after 24 hours of compression, she underwent intraoperative 
debridement and VAC placement.  Please see operative report for 
further details.  A urine culture sent by the ED returned w/ 
multidrug resistant E.coli x 2, both sensitive to meropenem.  By 
POD 1, her Cr had decreased to 1.0.  She was restarted on her 
oral hypoglycemics.  On POD 2, her VAC was removed; we noted 
clean, healthy granulation tissue at the base of the wound.  A 
PICC was placed.

At the time of discharge, the patient was afebrile with stable 
vital signs.  She was tolerating a regular diet, voiding without 
assistance, and her pain was well controlled.  Her wound was 
dressed with a wet-to-dry gauze, which will be replaced by a VAC 
once she reaches her rehab facility.  She will complete a 7 day 
course of meropenem.  She will be readmitted to undergo skin 
grafting; Dr. ___ will call her rehab facility 
with the date.  The patient received discharge teaching and 
follow-up instructions with understanding verbalized and 
agreement with the discharge plan.

Traumatic wound right lower leg

 
Discharge Condition:
Mental Status: Clear and coherent.
Level of Consciousness: Alert and interactive.
Activity Status: Ambulatory - requires assistance or aid (walker 
or cane).

 
Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the Vascular Surgery service for evaluation 
and treatment of your right leg wound. You underwent debridement 
of the wound in the operating room and placing of a vacuum 
assisted dressing. You tolerated this well and are now 
discharged to rehab to continue your recovery.  We will schedule 
you for readmission for skin grafting; Dr. ___ 
will call you with the date.  Please follow the following 
instructions:

Please call your doctor or nurse practitioner if you experience 
the following:
*You experience new chest pain, pressure, squeezing or 
tightness.
*New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or wheeze.
*If you are vomiting and cannot keep down fluids or your 
medications.
*You are getting dehydrated due to continued vomiting, diarrhea, 
or other reasons. Signs of dehydration include dry mouth, rapid 
heartbeat, or feeling dizzy or faint when standing.
*You see blood or dark/black material when you vomit or have a 
bowel movement.
*You experience burning when you urinate, have blood in your 
urine, or experience a discharge.
*Your pain is not improving within ___ hours or is not gone 
within 24 hours. Call or return immediately if your pain is 
getting worse or changes location or moving to your chest or 
back.
*You have shaking chills, or fever greater than 101.5 degrees 
Fahrenheit or 38 degrees Celsius.
*Any change in your symptoms, or any new symptoms that concern 
you.
.
General Discharge Instructions:
Please resume all regular home medications , unless specifically 
advised not to take a particular medication.  Also, please take 
any new medications as prescribed.
Please get plenty of rest, continue to ambulate several times 
per day, and drink adequate amounts of fluids.  Avoid driving or 
operating heavy machinery while taking pain medications.
Please follow-up with your surgeon and Primary Care Provider 
(PCP) as advised.
Wound Care:
*Please call your doctor or nurse practitioner if you have 
increased pain, swelling, redness, or drainage from the wound 
site.
*Avoid swimming and baths until your follow-up appointment.
*You may shower, and water may wash over the wound, but do not 
directly spray or scrub.  Gently pat the area dry.
*Weigh yourself every morning, call MD if weight goes up more 
than 3 lbs.
